lessons.title: God Said: Let There Be Light
lessons.big_truth: God made everything by His word, and everything He made was good.
lessons.christ_connection: The same Word that said 'Let there be light' became a person — Jesus (John 1:1-5). Jesus is the light that darkness can never put out.
lessons.obedience_step: Tonight when you see a light turn on, say thank You to God who made light.
lessons.multiply_step: Tell one person in your family the story of the first day, in your own words.

steps.body: Before anything existed — before the sun, before the sea, before you — God was there. And God spoke. He didn't need tools or helpers. He just said, 'Let there be light,' and light came running.
Look at the beam of light on your screen. Real light is faster and brighter than anything — and God made it with only His voice.
Build the memory verse, one glowing word at a time.
Say the memory verse out loud three times, a little quieter each time, until it is a whisper you can keep.
God's word is powerful. When God says something, it happens. You can trust everything He says.

lessons.title: The Shepherd Who Looks for the Lost
lessons.big_truth: God is like a shepherd who never gives up looking for His lost sheep.
lessons.christ_connection: Jesus told this story about Himself. He is the Good Shepherd who left heaven to find us and carry us home (John 10:11).
lessons.obedience_step: Pray for one friend who doesn't know Jesus yet — the Shepherd is looking for them.
lessons.multiply_step: Act out the lost-sheep story with a stuffed animal for someone younger than you.

steps.body: A shepherd counted his sheep: ...97, 98, 99 — one was missing! Did he say 'ninety-nine is plenty'? Never. He walked into the dark hills, calling and searching, until the lost one was found and safe on his shoulders.
Lead the lamb along the Shepherd's Path.
Memory verse: 'The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.'
When you feel lost or afraid, remember: the Shepherd knows your name and He is already looking for you.

lessons.title: One Big Story
lessons.big_truth: The whole Bible — from the very first page — is one story that leads to Jesus.
lessons.christ_connection: Creation, the promise, the kings, the prophets — every part of the story points ahead to Jesus, the Rescuer God promised.
lessons.obedience_step: Ask a grown-up to show you their favorite Bible story and find where it sits on the timeline.
lessons.multiply_step: Teach the order of the big story (Creation → Promise → Jesus → Church) to a friend using your fingers.

steps.body: The Bible is not a box of little stories. It is one river, flowing from the garden all the way to Jesus and then out to the whole world.
Place the great events on the river of light, in order.
Memory verse: 'Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.'
Every time you read the Bible, ask the treasure question: where is Jesus in this story?

lessons.title: The Greatest Gift
lessons.big_truth: God loved the world so much that He gave His only Son, so that everyone who believes in Him has life forever.
lessons.christ_connection: This IS the gospel: Jesus died for our sins and rose again. Believing in Him is not earning a prize — it is receiving a gift.
lessons.obedience_step: Talk to God in your own words: thank Him for giving Jesus, and tell Him you want to follow Him.
lessons.multiply_step: John 3:16 is good news for every person on earth. Who will you share it with this week? Say their name out loud.

steps.body: A gift is not a gift if you have to pay for it. God gave the most precious gift there ever was — His own Son — so that we could come home to Him.
Build John 3:16 — the verse missionaries have carried to every nation.
Say John 3:16 and put your own name in it: 'For God so loved ______...'
You never have to make God love you. He already did the loving first (Romans 5:8).

studies.title: The Word Became Flesh
studies.big_truth: Jesus is not merely a messenger from God; He is God the Son, the eternal Word, who entered His own creation.
studies.christ_connection: John deliberately opens with Genesis 1 language ('In the beginning') to declare that the Creator has become the Redeemer. The Word who spoke light now shines as the Light.
studies.context: John writes so that 'you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God' (John 20:31). 'Logos' (Word) spoke both to Jewish readers (God's creative word, Gen 1; Ps 33:6) and to Greek readers (the rational principle behind the cosmos). John claims both streams find their fulfillment in a person.
dbs: What does this passage say about God?
What does it say about people (vv. 5, 10-12)?
What must change in how I live if the Word truly 'dwelt among us'?
Who will I share this passage with before our next meeting?
studies.apologetic: Objection: 'Jesus never claimed to be God.' John 1:1-3,14 — written within living memory of eyewitnesses — asserts full deity and full humanity. See also John 8:58, 20:28. The earliest Christians worshiped Jesus as God at the cost of their lives; that conviction was not a later legend.
studies.obedience_step: Memorize John 1:1-5 this week and recite it to your group.
studies.multiply_step: Lead one person through vv. 1-14 using the four discovery questions above. You do not need to be an expert; the questions do the work.

studies.title: The Righteousness We Could Not Earn
studies.big_truth: All have sinned; God justifies sinners freely through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, received by faith.
studies.christ_connection: The 'Romans Road' is the gospel in four stones: universal guilt (3:23), demonstrated love (5:8), wages vs. gift (6:23), and the confession of faith (10:9). Christ's cross is where God's justice and mercy meet.
studies.context: Paul writes to a mixed Jewish-Gentile church he has not yet visited, laying out the gospel systematically. Chapters 1-3 establish that no one — religious or pagan — is righteous before God by works.
dbs: What do these verses say about God's character — both His justice and His love?
What do they say about every human being, including me?
What is the difference between a wage and a gift, and why does it matter for salvation?
Who in my life still thinks salvation must be earned? How will I show them these verses?
studies.apologetic: Objection: 'A loving God wouldn't judge sin.' Love without justice is indifference. Romans 5:8 shows God satisfying His own justice at His own cost — the judge stepped down and took the sentence Himself.
studies.obedience_step: Write out the four Romans Road verses on a card (or in your notes here) and practice sharing them in under five minutes.
studies.multiply_step: Share the Romans Road with one person this week. Record their name in your multiplication ledger and keep praying for them.

studies.title: Sent Ones: The Commission and the Church
studies.big_truth: The risen King commands His people to make disciples of all nations — and discipleship is designed to multiply through four generations.
studies.christ_connection: The Commission rests entirely on Christ's authority ('All authority... has been given to me') and His presence ('I am with you always'). Mission is not our project for God; it is Christ's own work through us.
studies.context: Matthew ends where the church begins. 2 Timothy 2:2 shows the mechanism: Paul → Timothy → faithful ones → others also. Four generations in one verse. A church is planted when disciples gather around the Word, baptize, break bread, and raise their own leaders (Acts 2:42-47; Titus 1:5).
dbs: What has Jesus been given, and what does that mean for the nations — and for my neighborhood?
What exactly are we commanded to do: make converts, or make disciples who obey? What is the difference?
What would a simple church look like in my home or village — Word, prayer, bread, baptism, leaders?
Name your 'Timothy' — the person you are training who will train others. If you have none, who could be the first?
studies.apologetic: Objection: 'Mission is cultural imperialism.' The gospel is the one message that dignifies every culture equally: every nation, tribe, and tongue is invited as-is to the same table (Rev 7:9). Church-planting done biblically raises LOCAL leaders and puts the Word in LOCAL hands — this app exists to make itself unnecessary.
studies.obedience_step: Begin the 3/3rds pattern with your group this week: Look Back (accountability), Look Up (new passage), Look Forward (goal and prayer).
studies.multiply_step: Open your multiplication ledger and write the names of your first generation. Pray over each name daily.

vocab.teaching: In John 1, the eternal self-expression of God — not merely speech about God, but God the Son Himself. Used ~330x in the NT.
The status of being in the right before God. Romans' central theme: a righteousness from God, given to sinners through faith in Christ (Rom 3:21-26).
God's free, undeserved kindness — the opposite of wages. Grace is not God ignoring sin, but God paying for it Himself.
The called-out gathering of Christ's people — never a building in the NT, always a people. The goal of missions is planting these worshiping communities everywhere.
God's loyal, promise-keeping love — the 'goodness and mercy' that pursues David in Psalm 23:6. Fulfilled in Christ, who keeps covenant for us.
